slides.title: Model Capacity Frontier: A Development Framework for LLM-Supported Social Simulation
slides.highlight: The Model Capacity Frontier framework addresses configuration sensitivity in LLM-supported agent-based models, offering a method to systematically evaluate architectural limits in large-scale social simulations relevant to MIMIC's goal of modeling hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Framework using Pareto frontiers to distinguish configuration tuning from architectural limits in LLM simulations.
card.key_idea: Characterizes attainable empirical performance across admissible configurations via Pareto frontiers, separating configuration sensitivity from architectural capacity.
card.evaluation: Validated on 12,000-agent crowd simulation using video data; metrics include temporal occupancy, spatial distribution, and flow direction.
card.limitation: Requires extensive computational resources for sampling; frontier estimates remain conservative due to sparse configuration exploration.

slides.title: Gossip Agents: Reputation through Opinion Dynamics over Evolving Networks
slides.highlight: This work models reputation diffusion through gossip and opinion dynamics in evolving networks, offering insights into how information propagation mechanisms can sustain cooperation in hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Gossip-based reputation diffusion via opinion dynamics promotes cooperation in dynamic multi-agent networks.
card.key_idea: Agents form private opinions from local observations and exchange them via DeGroot dynamics over evolving networks, controlled by a tunable broadcast radius.
card.evaluation: Tested on n-player Prisoner's Dilemma and Harvest using DQN; compared against no-reputation baselines across varying broadcast radii.
card.limitation: Relies on fixed, hand-crafted assessment rules for prosocial/antisocial behavior rather than learned evaluation policies.

slides.title: Towards Adaptive and Real-Survey-Aligned Simulated Urban Mobility Behaviour of Generative Agents
slides.highlight: This paper evaluates generative agents for simulating multimodal urban mobility, demonstrating their ability to adapt to unforeseen events and align with real survey data, which is relevant to MIMIC's goal of modeling human-AI societal interactions at a meso-scale.

card.one_liner: Generative agents match aggregate modal splits of survey-fitted models but fail individual trip accuracy.
card.key_idea: LLM-based agents with tuned prompts simulate urban mobility, leveraging built-in knowledge to react to unforeseen textual events.
card.evaluation: Compared 15 decision-makers on 3,299 Toulouse trips using modal split divergence and trip-level accuracy against survey baselines.
card.limitation: Agents achieve realistic aggregate splits but assign lower probability to actual reported modes than traditional models.

slides.title: Beyond Two Tracks: Speaker-Anchored Full-Duplex Dialogue Recovery
slides.tldr: SPEAKER-ANCHORED TRACK ROUTING FOR FULL-DUPLEX RECOVERY
slides.highlight: This work addresses the challenge of maintaining consistent speaker identities in full-duplex dialogue recovery, a critical requirement for accurate diarization and addressee modeling in hybrid human-AI team state perception.

card.one_liner: Speaker-anchored routing before diffusion ensures persistent participant identity in full-duplex dialogue recovery.
card.key_idea: A lightweight router matches separator streams to enrollment anchors before a frozen generator, fixing track assignments without retraining.
card.evaluation: Tested on CANDOR, Seamless, and SpokenWOZ; reduced wrong-track time to 4.1% while preserving audio quality and enabling domain transfer.
card.limitation: Requires enrollment speech for anchors; performance relies on coarse stream quality, though verification mitigates low-margin errors.

slides.title: Sensitivity Analysis of Decision Rules in an Agent-Based Agro-Ecological Model
slides.highlight: This work introduces a method for sensitivity analysis in agent-based models with hierarchical decision structures, addressing the challenge of parameters that are conditional on higher-level choices. It is relevant to MIMIC for improving the interpretability and robustness of simulations involving complex, multi-scale agent behaviors.

card.one_liner: Proposes a structure-aware sensitivity analysis for hierarchical agro-ecological agent-based models.
card.key_idea: Combines random-forest supervision with HSIC-ANOVA on a hierarchical design space to rank decision effects without imputing inactive parameters.
card.evaluation: Applied to MAELIA simulator outputs (nitrogen leaching, carbon, yield) using 5,000 simulations; yields interpretable, decision-oriented rankings.
card.limitation: Requires computationally intensive surrogate training and may struggle with extremely high-dimensional spaces despite pruning.

slides.title: Persona AI Brings Calm Experience to Humanoid Startups
slides.highlight: Persona AI's focus on calm experiences for humanoid startups aligns with RwB's goal of developing embodied social robots for positive human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Context Matters! Social, Spatial, and Semantic Coordination with an Embodied Agent in Immersive Analytics
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a framework for context-aware design of embodied agents in AR, focusing on spatial, social, and semantic dimensions, which informs strategies for natural human-robot interaction in embodied learning settings.

card.one_liner: Proposes a spatial, social, and semantic context framework for embodied AI agents in immersive analytics.
card.key_idea: Introduces a conceptual framework categorizing context into spatial, social, and semantic dimensions, split by embeddedness and awareness.
card.evaluation: Validated via Cobot, a design probe on HoloLens 2, using reflective use-case scenarios rather than quantitative user studies.
card.limitation: The framework is preliminary, single-user focused, and lacks empirical validation of specific contextual factors' impact.

slides.title: GCAM-Gym: A Benchmark for Agent-Based Climate Policy Search
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a standardized Gymnasium environment for evaluating agent-based climate policy search methods, offering a rigorous framework for comparing control systems under varying feedback and budget constraints.

card.one_liner: GCAM-Gym benchmarks climate policy search, showing CMA-ES outperforms other methods in finding cost-effective 2°C targets.
card.key_idea: A Gymnasium-compatible interface for GCAM supporting full-policy and stepwise control, evaluating seven search systems across three settings.
card.evaluation: Compared seven systems using 3,210 GCAM evaluations; CMA-ES achieved highest IQM returns, though runtime defects affect result validity.
card.limitation: Runtime measurement issues and unvalidated temperature thresholds compromise the reliability of reported policy outcomes and method rankings.

slides.title: The GenAI Who Knew Too Little: Revisiting Transactive Memory Systems in Human GenAI Collaboration
slides.highlight: This study examines how Transactive Memory Systems differ in human-GenAI collaboration, highlighting asymmetric expertise recognition and hierarchical coordination, which informs HyECHO's modeling of hybrid team dynamics and social perception.

card.one_liner: Qualitative study reveals asymmetric transactive memory dynamics in human-GenAI collaboration.
card.key_idea: Analyzes TMS dimensions: asymmetric expertise recognition, ambivalent trust with verification, and hierarchical coordination.
card.evaluation: Qualitative interpretive interviews with 14 knowledge workers; thematic analysis of TMS manifestations.
card.limitation: Small sample size (n=14) limits generalizability; findings are qualitative rather than quantitative.

slides.title: SocialCoAct: Enabling and Benchmarking Egocentric Social Co-Action for VLM-Based Humanoid Robots
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework and benchmark for egocentric social co-action, addressing the need for high-level semantic planning and awareness of complex social environments in humanoid agents. It is relevant to HyECHO's goal of multimodal social perception by providing methods to align verbal responses with atomic action sequences in multi-party interactions.

card.one_liner: SocialCoAct enables VLM-based humanoid robots to coordinate speech and actions in egocentric social interactions.
card.key_idea: Framework transforms egocentric observations into aligned verbal responses and atomic action sequences, evaluated via a new multi-task benchmark.
card.evaluation: 423 human-verified MCQs from egocentric datasets; tested on 15 VLMs, showing best accuracy of 77.54% and hard subset at 46.51%.
card.limitation: Extended reasoning improves accuracy but drastically reduces inference speed, hindering real-time responsiveness for online social agents.

slides.title: RoboMMT: Learning Stable Tracking of Modulated Expressive and Interactive Robot Motion
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a control architecture that enables dynamically unstable robots to execute expressive motions while maintaining stability, directly supporting RwB's goal of natural human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: RoboMMT enables stable, expressive robot motion by coupling parameterized synthesis with physics-based tracking and reactive goal modulation.
card.key_idea: A modular architecture trains a reference-conditioned tracking policy over a broad expressive domain, then layers lightweight interaction policies to modulate spatial goals.
card.evaluation: Tested on quadruped and humanoid robots in simulation and real hardware, demonstrating high stability, accurate tracking, and zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.
card.limitation: The method does not address how expressivity is generated or perceived, requiring separate user studies for social effectiveness validation.

slides.title: JR West Unveils Humanoid Robots
slides.highlight: JR West's introduction of humanoid robots highlights the growing integration of embodied agents in public service environments, offering a real-world context for studying human-robot interaction and social robotics applications.

slides.title: Machina Pauliana: A neuro-symbolic approach to the actio pauliana in Dutch insolvency law
slides.highlight: This paper demonstrates a neuro-symbolic architecture for legal reasoning, combining symbolic rule-based logic with neural components for open-textured terms, which aligns with MIMIC's use of neuro-symbolic agent models for complex societal simulations.

card.one_liner: A neuro-symbolic model for Dutch insolvency law combines Catala rules with LLM-based case retrieval.
card.key_idea: Catala symbolic core handles logic; neural routines extract facts and resolve open-textured terms via RAG over segmented Dutch judgments.
card.evaluation: Segmentation/labelling scored high on 100 judgments; end-to-end tested on 10 hard cases, showing moderate accuracy and knowledge-requirement struggles.
card.limitation: Evaluated only on 10 contested cases; routine extrajudicial settlements are absent, limiting generalizability to typical insolvency practice.

slides.title: Moss Intelligence Raises $149 Million Pre-A in Push for Real-Time Multimodal AI
slides.highlight: Moss Intelligence's funding for real-time multimodal AI aligns with HyECHO's focus on non-data-hungry multimodal social perception of hybrid human-AI team states.
